issues.title: EPIC: HC-P1 Information Architecture and Coverage Map

issues.body:
## Objective
Apply cross-cutting polish and quality gates so the UI feels production-ready and reliable.

## Parent Epic
- #56 (EPIC-7)

## Depends On
- #59 (U3)
- #60 (U4)
- #61 (U5)
- #62 (U6)
- #63 (U7)
- #64 (U8)
- #65 (U9)
- #66 (U10)
- #67 (U11)
- #68 (U12)
- #69 (U13)
- #70 (U14)

## Implementation Plan
1. Standardize destructive-action confirmations and success/failure toasts across all pages.
2. Add loading skeletons and explicit empty states for every list/table/report panel.
3. Introduce route-level and widget-level error boundaries with recovery actions.
4. Run accessibility remediation (labels, roles, focus order, keyboard reachability, contrast checks).
5. Add final smoke checks for window resize/scaling and packaged runtime behavior.

## Test Plan
1. Unit: empty/loading/error state component contracts and fallback rendering paths.
2. Integration: action failures surface recoverable error banners without app crash.
3. Accessibility automation: axe checks on major routes; keyboard tab-flow test suite.
4. E2E smoke: packaged app workflow from dashboard -> import -> alerts -> reports -> settings with no uncaught renderer errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All primary pages have consistent loading, empty, and error handling UX.
- [ ] Destructive actions require confirmation and show outcome feedback.

UIReply.md identified a monolithic renderer UI with weak information architecture and prototype-level interactions. This epic delivers a first-class desktop UI with routed app shell, workflow-centric pages, consistent design system, and keyboard-first usability.

2. Maintain shared UI patterns and architecture constraints across all child implementations.
3. Run milestone-level regression checks before closing the epic.
